questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion with the passive voice and a negative subjunctive clause?
options: It was not until she had finished reading the report that the director was informed of its findings.
Only when the meeting was over did he realise he had missed the bus.
Had the project been completed earlier, more resources would have been allocated to it.
No sooner had the team arrived than they were dismissed for poor performance.
questions.answer: Had the project been completed earlier, more resources would have been allocated to it.

questions.question: Which sentence employs a cleft construction to express emphasis on the *reason* for an action?
options: What surprised me was that he had forgotten my birthday again.
The reason she left the company was because of the toxic work environment.
It was in Paris that I first met my future wife.
The fact that he arrived late was entirely due to his own carelessness.
questions.answer: It was in Paris that I first met my future wife.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a third conditional with a subjunctive auxiliary (*were*) to discuss hypothetical past circumstances?
options: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
If he had known the rules, he wouldn’t have made that mistake.
If they had invited me, I would have come with them.
If we had won the lottery, we would have bought a house in the countryside.
questions.answer: If he had known the rules, he wouldn’t have made that mistake.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates the use of ellipsis in a formal context to avoid repetition?
options: She said she’d be back in time for dinner, and she kept her word.
He didn’t come to the meeting, and neither did his colleague.
The report was submitted on time, and the deadline was extended accordingly.
They argued about the project’s scope, and eventually, they agreed on a compromise.
questions.answer: The report was submitted on time, and the deadline was extended accordingly.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a formal register with a nuanced choice of verb (*ought to*) to express obligation with a conditional clause?
options: He ought to have finished his homework before leaving the house.
She ought to have contacted the authorities sooner to report the theft.
They ought to have been more cautious with the data, given the security risks.
We ought to have considered the environmental impact before building the dam.
questions.answer: She ought to have contacted the authorities sooner to report the theft.
